distinguishing_construction.space: The real line with its usual metric and Lebesgue measure, so mu(B(c,R))=2R for R>0.
distinguishing_construction.phases: Theta={theta_0,theta_1}, where theta_0(x)=0 and theta_1(x)=x. Both continuous functions vanish at 0.
distinguishing_construction.auxiliary_distances: For positive radius R, set d_B(theta_0,theta_1)=2^18 R and diagonal distances to zero. Use the zero pseudometric for nonpositive radii.
compatibility_checks: The real line is complete and locally compact with a nonzero locally finite Borel measure; mu(B(c,2R))=2 mu(B(c,R))<=16 mu(B(c,R)).
For different phases the local oscillation is 2R<=2^18 R. Equal phases have zero oscillation.
Inclusion of nonempty real balls implies monotonicity of radii and thus of the distances. Empty balls have zero distances.
Radius dilation by 2 multiplies the phase distance by 2<=16, independently of the center; dilation by 16 multiplies it by 16>=2. These establish both scale comparison conditions.
Every phase ball is covered by at most two balls of any positive radius, hence by at most 16; nonpositive-radius balls are empty.
informal_cancellative_proof: For a globally Lipschitz complex function phi supported in B(c,R), let M=sup_B |phi|, L=Lip_B(phi), and N=M+R L. Continuity and vanishing outside the open ball give phi(c-R)=phi(c+R)=0 and M<=R L.

For the distinct phase pair, the direct bound gives |integral_B exp(ix)phi(x) dx|<=2R M<=R N. Lipschitz functions on the interval are absolutely continuous; integration by parts with zero endpoint values gives a second bound 2R L<=2N.
Consequently the integral norm is at most 2R N min(1/2,1/R). For 0<R<=2, 1+2^18 R<=1+2^19<2^20=(2*16)^4, so 1/2<=16/(1+2^18 R)^(1/4).
For R>=2, 1+2^18 R<=2^19 R<=2^16 R^4, so 1/R<=16/(1+2^18 R)^(1/4). This proves the required informal estimate at every positive radius and center.
The reversed pair uses exp(-ix) and the same estimates. Equal phases satisfy the trivial bound by mu(B) M<=16 mu(B) N.

formal_failure.test: phi=1_B, viewed as complex-valued. Function.support(phi)=B, and iLipENorm(phi,0,1)=1 because phi is constant on B.

remaining_hypotheses.kernel: K(x,y)=0 is measurable and satisfies the size and regularity estimates.
remaining_hypotheses.boundedness: T_* g=0 for every g, so the required bounded strong (2,2) estimate holds.
remaining_hypotheses.interpretation: The zero kernel satisfies the other theorem hypotheses. This is a counterexample to equivalence of the fixed-structure cancellative assumptions, not a counterexample to the main conclusion.

limitations: Auxiliary distances and a are fixed. No impossibility of alternative auxiliary-distance encodings is established.
